parsed.headline: President Mahama proposes routes to South America and Caribbean for Ghana’s planned national airline

pages.text: President John Mahama has indicated that Ghana’s proposed national airline may explore routes to South America and the Caribbean to facilitate trade, tourism, investment, and people-to-people exchanges. During bilateral talks with Suriname’s President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons in New York on September 23, 2026, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, President Mahama suggested that connectivity with these regions could form part of the carrier's future route network. This follows an August visit to Jamaica, where the Presidency announced on August 3, 2026, that President Mahama and Jamaican Prime Minister Andrew Holness agreed to accelerate work on a Bilateral Air Services Agreement to facilitate direct flights between Accra and Montego Bay once concluded.

The proposed expansion has raised questions regarding whether available traffic data and the size of the potential passenger market support such routes. According to the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority’s 2025 international aviation statistics, Ghana recorded 2,539,034 international passenger movements that year, consisting of 1,238,220 arrivals and 1,300,814 departures. These plans come as Ghana confronts drug-trafficking cases. The 2026 World Drug Report identifies Colombia, Peru, and Brazil as main departure countries for cocaine shipments recorded between 2020 and 2024, noting that Brazil is also featured in trafficking routes to Africa and Europe.

parsed.headline: Speaker Bagbin backs President Mahama's call for national dialogue on hate speech

pages.text: Speaker of Parliament Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin has expressed support for President John Dramani Mahama’s call for a national dialogue regarding hate speech and abusive online content. Addressing an emergency sitting of Parliament on September 29, 2026, Mr. Bagbin described the President's call as timely and necessary for the protection of Ghana’s democratic culture. This follows a request made by President Mahama the previous week to the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) and the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) to convene a national stakeholder engagement. The proposed initiative aims to develop a national roadmap to address abusive, insulting, threatening, and hateful speech—particularly on social media and digital platforms—while protecting freedom of expression.

parsed.headline: Flydubai pilot allegedly stabs co-pilot during flight from UAE to Israel

pages.text: A Flydubai Boeing 737 traveling from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Israel was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia following an alleged altercation between its pilots, according to reports from The Guardian World. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that one of the pilots stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to be attempting to crash the aircraft. Netanyahu described the event as an extremely severe security incident. An Israeli official identified the attacker as an Omani national, as reported by Reuters. Israeli officials are investigating whether the incident constituted an attempted terror attack on Israelis. Defense Minister Israel Katz and other officials have also characterized the event as an attempted terrorist attack. During the incident, the plane reportedly descended approximately 16,000 feet in two minutes while over Jordan. The aircraft transmitted three emergency signals, including one indicating possible unlawful interference, approximately two and a half hours after departing Dubai, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24. Fearing a hijacking attempt on a plane carrying between 160 and 180 passengers, including dozens of Israelis, Israeli officials scrambled fighter jets. The plane landed at Tabuk airport in north-western Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu reported that a passenger and a crew member managed to break into the cockpit and neutralize the attacking pilot, praising the individuals for their resourcefulness and courage.

parsed.headline: Syria to include Kobani and Rojava universities in general admissions process

pages.text: Syrian Higher Education and Scientific Research Minister Marwan al-Halabi announced that colleges at Kobani University and Rojava University in Qamishli will be included in the general university admissions process for the 2026-2027 academic year. According to al-Halabi, this move is part of efforts to unify higher education institutions and the admissions system under the ministry. A ministerial committee has begun assessing Kobani University to prepare for its integration with Aleppo University, a process al-Halabi noted is similar to the previous integration of al-Sharq University in Raqqa with Euphrates University. The committee is currently reviewing academic, scientific, administrative, and technical aspects, including curricula, teaching systems, infrastructure, laboratories, and student and staff numbers.

Al-Halabi stated that degrees issued by Kobani University will be recognized and certified without modification, allowing graduates to practice professions related to their specializations throughout Syria in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The integration process is intended to include any academic program, faculty member, or administrator that meets required standards. Work will focus on accrediting programs and integrating administrative staff and faculty members according to established rules. Al-Halabi added that Kobani University students will be treated like other Syrian students, with their academic rights and educational continuity protected under the Higher Education Organization Law. The minister stated that unifying these institutions aims to establish a single academic authority and ensure equal opportunities for students while protecting the rights of institutions, academic programs, and qualified staff.

parsed.headline: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang attends inaugural GAAS Women’s Awards

pages.text: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang attended the inaugural Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences (GAAS) Women’s Awards on September 30, 2026. Held under the theme “Breaking Barriers, Building Nations: Celebrating Women in Outstanding Leadership in Ghana,” the event recognized women for their contributions to leadership and national development across various sectors. According to MyJoyOnline, Dr. Opoku-Agyemang has been a Fellow of the Academy for approximately two decades. During the ceremony, the Vice President noted that women have contributed to Ghana's economic and social foundations through activities such as farming, fishing, trading, healing, and community leadership since long before gender equality became a central part of national discourse. While acknowledging progress in promoting opportunities for women, she stated that the representation of women within institutions like the Academy indicates that further work is required. Dr. Opoku-Agyemang commended the Academy for recognizing women making impacts at the grassroots level and emphasized the need for deliberate measures to remove barriers to women's participation. She cited expanded access to education, gender equity measures, and improved access to finance, including initiatives like the Women’s Development Bank, as interventions for creating greater opportunities.

parsed.headline: Syrian authorities foil attempt to smuggle 225,000 Captagon pills

pages.text: Syrian anti-narcotics forces in the Damascus countryside, working alongside border guards, foiled an attempt to smuggle 225,000 Captagon pills from Lebanon, according to authorities on Wednesday. The General Directorate for Drug Control stated via its official social media accounts that the operation was the result of field surveillance and monitoring. Two individuals, identified by the initials M.H. and M.H., were arrested in connection with the smuggling operation. The directorate reported that the seized drugs were confiscated and the two suspects were referred to the relevant judicial authorities for further investigation and legal action.

parsed.headline: University of Ghana Pro-Vice-Chancellor calls for increased research funding to address brain drain

pages.text: Prof. Gordon Akanzuwine Awandare, the Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs at the University of Ghana, has called for stronger and sustained investment in science and research. Speaking on September 29, 2026, at the UGMC Research Symposium, themed “From Bench to Bedside: Integrating Research, Technology, and Clinical Care in Ghana,” Awandare warned that inadequate funding and weak research ecosystems contribute to brain drain and limit Africa’s capacity for cutting-edge scientific research. He stated that African governments must demonstrate commitment through actual budgetary allocations, noting that current budgetary figures often do not match official rhetoric regarding science and research. Awandare identified poor remuneration for scientists and researchers, alongside a weak research ecosystem, as factors contributing to the loss of intellectual talent and skilled professionals. He further noted that Africa's ability to conduct discovery research has been constrained by the high costs associated with basic and fundamental research, specifically citing the expensive infrastructure required for fields such as genomics and drug discovery, including equipment like NMR machines, mass spectrometers, and genome sequencing tools.

parsed.headline: Akyem Hemang residents protest following death of man allegedly shot by suspected military personnel

pages.text: On September 29, 2026, residents of Akyem Hemang and surrounding communities in the Fanteakwa South District staged a street protest demanding justice for Douglas Acheampong. Acheampong, a 29-year-old resident, was allegedly shot and killed at an illegal mining site near Osino in the Eastern Region on August 26, 2026. According to Graphic Online, protesters wearing red armbands and carrying placards with messages such as “Douglas deserves justice” and “Military must serve not kill” marched through the streets to present a petition to the Fanteakwa South District Chief Executive, Mercy Korang. The protesters are demanding the arrest of the alleged killers of Acheampong. Local Assembly Member Richmond Darko alleged that Acheampong was shot from behind while fleeing the scene after security personnel reportedly fired warning shots into a crowd. Darko called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances of the death to ensure those responsible face the law.

Following the receipt of the petition, District Chief Executive Mercy Korang assured protesters that their concerns would be forwarded to President Mahama and other appropriate quarters to ensure justice is taken. Korang appealed to the protesters and local residents to remain calm and patient while the matter is addressed through appropriate channels.

parsed.headline: Hezbollah denies connection to three-member cell detained in Syria’s Daraa governorate

pages.text: Hezbollah’s media relations office issued a statement on Wednesday rejecting claims of affiliation with a three-member cell detained by Syrian authorities in the Daraa governorate. The group categorically denied any relationship or connection with the cell, stating it has no presence in Syria and is not involved in any security or military activity within the country, according to reporting by North Press Agency. This denial follows an announcement by Syria’s General Intelligence Directorate and Internal Security Forces regarding the arrest of three individuals in the Yarmouk Basin in western Daraa. Syrian authorities identified the detainees by the initials F.K., Z.M., and L.A., stating the operation occurred after surveillance of an alleged attempt by the cell to prepare rocket-launch platforms for attacks. Authorities reported that the launch platforms had been dismantled.
